neighborhoods.name: Old San Juan (Viejo San Juan)
neighborhoods.tip: The walled old city: hilly, with blue cobblestones. Taxis wait by Plaza Colón and the cruise piers, and Uber picks up on the main streets.

neighborhoods.name: Condado
neighborhoods.tip: A walkable strip of hotels, restaurants and the calm Condado lagoon. Fixed taxi fare to and from the airport; Uber is easy here.

neighborhoods.name: Ocean Park
neighborhoods.tip: A quiet beach neighborhood between Condado and Isla Verde. Uber is the easy option; the airport taxi fare is fixed.

neighborhoods.name: Isla Verde (Carolina)
neighborhoods.tip: Beach hotels about 10 minutes from the airport, with a fixed taxi fare. Old San Juan is 20 to 30 minutes by car.

neighborhoods.name: Santurce and Miramar
neighborhoods.tip: Murals, galleries and food, lively at night around La Placita. Take a ride home late rather than walking far.

neighborhoods.name: Elsewhere in the metro area (Guaynabo, Bayamón, Río Piedras…)
neighborhoods.tip: Uber covers the whole metro area; fixed taxi fares only cover the tourist zones.

airports.name: San Juan airport (Luis Muñoz Marín, SJU)
airports.tip: Tourist taxis wait outside baggage claim. The dispatcher tells you the fixed fare before you get in. Uber picks up at its marked zone.

items.title: Uber
items.text: Uber is the island’s main ride app (Discover Puerto Rico), easy around San Juan and at the airport. Getting back from farther places is the hard part: ride apps can’t operate inside El Yunque, and drivers are scarce outside the metro area at night.

items.title: Tourist taxis
items.text: White Taxi Turístico cabs wait at the airport, the cruise piers, hotels and big sights. Fares between the airport and the tourist zones are fixed; pay in cash, and agree the fare first for anything else.

items.title: Day trips need a ride both ways
items.text: For El Yunque, Luquillo and the bio bay, book a tour with pickup or a driver for the day. Arrange the ride back before you go, especially over the holidays.

items.title: Walking
items.text: Old San Juan is compact but hilly, with blue cobblestones that get slippery in rain. The beach neighborhoods are flat; avoid walking long stretches between neighborhoods, especially at night.

items.title: Driving
items.text: A rental car is the easiest way to explore on your own, but city traffic and parking in Old San Juan are hard work. A tour or a driver avoids both.

getting_around.source: Discover Puerto Rico and the US Forest Service

taxis.intro_bold: Tourist taxis have fixed fares from the airport.
taxis.intro: Look for the white Taxi Turístico cabs at the airport, cruise piers, hotels and big sights, or ask your hotel to call one. Fares are paid in cash; tolls and tips aren’t included.
taxis.apps: Uber is the island’s main ride app and serves the airport. Lyft doesn’t operate here.

rides.title: Drivers and rides
rides.intro: Uber is easy around San Juan, but the rainforest, Luquillo and the bio bay need a ride arranged both ways. Book drivers and tours ahead, especially over the holidays.

items.name: Uber and Uber Reserve
items.what: The island’s main ride app. Uber Reserve books a ride ahead where it’s offered.

items.name: Luquillo Taxi & Tours
items.what: Family-run taxi, transfer and tour company since 2011. Describes itself as licensed and insured.
items.area: Old San Juan to Fajardo, the Ceiba ferry, Culebra and Vieques
items.note: For a full day, ask for the price in writing, the vehicle and number of seats, and the driver’s name.

rides.note: Listed because an official source names them, not because Wanderings has ridden with them. We found no published day rates, so ask for a quote. Hotels can also book licensed drivers they trust.
